correctness.rationale: The commutator line is homogeneous, since it is spanned by homogeneous brackets. Its degree gives a quotient decomposition V=U⊕W with the component containing the center equal to the full preimage of its quotient and the other component a graph of a linear functional. For even center, the mixed bracket must vanish, so U and W are nondegenerate orthogonal complements, and the Sp stabilizer and graph lifts give E_(n,r). For odd center both diagonal brackets must vanish. Thus U,W are complementary Lagrangians; their ordered pairs number prod_i(q^i+1) q^(n(n+1)/2), since complements of one Lagrangian are graphs of symmetric matrices (also in characteristic two). There are q^n graph lifts. Symplectic basis changes and central shears prove transitivity within, and center degree and dimensions distinguish, the asserted orbits. The even degree exponent is n(n+1)−(2r−n)(2r−n+1), with a unique integral maximum at r=floor(n/2). The odd exponent is n²+2n, giving the correction of order q^(−n) with coefficient −1. Inner adjoints square to zero in class two, so an idempotent one is zero. The n=1, q=4 check independently counts five quotient lines, giving odd 5·4·4=80 and even 16+1, total 97. The supplied reduced-echelon and bracket tester was inspected, not executed; the small count is corroboration, not a proof by enumeration.

broader_coverage.reasoning: In a homogeneous symplectic basis the pair degrees must sum to the central degree. For Z/2 there is thus one type per number r of even pairs with even center, and one type with opposite parities in every pair with odd center. The cited automorphism description enables the exact stabilizer count; the two other related scopes are not evidence for the frozen census.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For even center, preserving the two standard graded quotient summands requires block similitudes of a common multiplier; preserving the odd graph at zero requires the functional to vanish on W. Thus the stabilizer order is (q−1)s_r s_(n−r) q^(2r), versus (q−1)s_n q^(2n) for the whole group. Their quotient is exactly the even-center formula for the remaining fields. The proportion follows just by comparing degrees, and the obstruction to nonzero inner idempotents follows from the central image of every inner adjoint.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Projection onto the odd component is an idempotent derivation in characteristic two, with inverse D↦(ker D, im D), equivariantly. This is also a bijection between odd-center gradings and idempotent derivations acting as 1 on the center in odd characteristic: for an odd-center grading [H_1,H_1]=0 because it lies in both H_0 and the center; conversely an idempotent derivation imposes eigenvalue 2 on that bracket, so it vanishes in odd characteristic. Thus the correspondence is exact in those regimes, not just an analogy.
